newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - British Sunday papers - May 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - British Sunday papers - May 18.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
INDEPENDENT ON SUNDAY -- DEWAR'S HEADS FOR SELL-OFF

Guinness and Grand Metropolitan may have to sell Scotch and gin brands to get their merger past competition authorities. John McGrath, the chief executive of Grand Met who will assume the same role at the new company GMG Brands, was confident the deal would get approval from the European Commission and Federal Trade Commission or the Department of Justice in US. Top executives at Grand Met have been criticised by leading shareholders for the millions of pounds they are likely to make on options if the deal goes ahead.
-- MINISTER KEEPS HEAT ON PENSION FIRMS

New Treasury minister Helen Liddell has written to the worst-offending companies in the pensions mis-selling scandal saying she expects detailed policy statements by 16 June 1997. The tough approach is intended to kick-start the derailed compensation process which was introduced 18 months ago.
-- LUFTHANSA SALE GETS GREEN LIGHT

The German parliament is set to pass legislation to allow the German government to sell its remaining 37.5 per cent stake in Lufthansa by the summer. The Federal Transport Minister Matthias Wissmann also hinted that the sale would be followed by privatisation of German airports.
-- M&S BREAKS 1 BN STG BARRIER

Marks and Spencer is set to announce end of year profits of 1.11bn on Tuesday despite strong competition from other clothing retailers. M&S warned of disappointing growth in food sales earlier in the year because of price cuts and similar quality product lines from other retailers.
-- GLYNWED BOSS FEELS THE HEAT

Gareth Davies, chairman of Aga cookers, engineering and metals groups, is facing renewed calls from institutional shareholders to quit. Shareholders also want the Glynwed board of directors to review his decision to promote Tony Wilson to chief executive in one years time.
SUNDAY TIMES
-- FORMULA ONE FLOAT GETS GREEN LIGHT

Salomon Brothers is set to announce the flotation of Formula One, the international motor-racing business controlled by businessman Bernie Ecclestone, within the next few days. Formula One could come to the stock market in time for the British Grand Prix at Silverstone in July.
-- OFLOT'S DAVIS IS LIKELY TO GO NEXT YEAR

Peter Davis, head of Oflot, is unlikely to be reappointed by the new Labour government when his contract expires in October 1998. Davis was heavily criticised by MPs for accepting free flights from GTech, one of the shareholders in the Camelot consortium. Heritage Secretary Chris Smith is thought to be considering a review of Oflot's role.
-- BROWN SET TO RECRUIT FROM BUSINESS

The Chancellor Gordon Brown will announce a number of business task forces to improve Britain's economic performance at the Confederation of British Industry's annual dinner on Tuesday. The task forces will try to find ways of raising Britain's competitiveness and investment record.
-- BZW TOLD: BUCK UP OR FACE SURGERY

Senior sources at Barclays have told its investment banking subsidiary BZW it must improve its financial performance in the next 18 months or face radical changes. There had been speculation that Barclays were about to sell BZW with Commerzbank of Germany tipped as a likely buyer.
-- HARDING'S CHELSEA STAKE UP FOR SALE

Matthew Harding estate is rumoured to want Harding's stake in Chelsea Village, the holding company which owns the club. The shareholding of the former deputy chairman of Chelsea football club is thought to be worth about 50mn stg. Harding died last year in a helicopter crash.
THE OBSERVER
-- BROWN SET TO SIGNAL TOUGH BUDGET

The Chancellor Gordon Brown has heightened expectations of tax rises by announcing his intention for a tough Budget. He should signal the Labour Party's intention to involve more businessmen in government this week at the CBI's annual dinner after the appointment of former BP chairman Sir David Simon as minister for trade and competitiveness in Europe.
-- GMG DEAL DRIVES ALLIED DOMECQ TO SEEK PARTNER

The proposed merger between Guinness and Grand Metropolitan has forced Allied Domecq, the world's second biggest spirits company, to consider a merger or joint venture to compete. Allied Domecq has set up a task force, including Goldman Sachs and UBS, to consider its options.
-- BT 'MUST NOT PASS WINDFALL TAX TO CONSUMERS'

Paymaster general Geoffrey Robinson has told BT and other privatised utilities that the Labour government will not allow them to pass on the cost of the windfall tax to consumers through higher bills. Treasury officials expect to meet regulators in the next fortnight to discuss the tax.
-- SALE OF BP SHARES COULD BRING 280M STG TAX BILL

The Kuwait Investment Office (KIO) could face a 280m stg tax bill following its sale of 1.2bn stg of British Petroleum shares. The Inland Revenue has been investigating KIO stake in the company after allegations that the identity of the true owner, the Kuwait Petroleum Company, had been concealed from the UK authorities.
-- BA BOSS BACKS LABOUR'S 'POSITIVE' APPROACH

Bob Ayling, chief executive of British Airways, has backed the Labour government's proposals for a minimum wage and closer European integration. Ayling is also in favour of a single European currency although he thought it unlikely that Britain would be ready for the first wave in 1999.
SUNDAY TELEGRAPH
-- LONRHO IN MERGER TALKS WITH JCI

Lonrho Plc is considering an imaginative merger proposal from JCI, South Africa's first black-controlled mining and gold producer, which would create one of the world's largest mining companies. The deal has been approved by Anglo American Corp which recently sold its stake in JCI.
-- MERCEDES CHIEF TO HEAD F1

The former chairman of Mercedes Benz, Helmut Werner, is set to become chairman of Formula One, following its decision to float on the stock market this summer. Market sources had thought the chief executive of Formula One, Bernie Ecclestone, and Salomon Brothers were going to delay or even cancel the planned flotation.
-- MOBIL AND AMOCO PLAN 20BN DOLLAR LINK

Two of America's leading oil companies, Mobil and Amoco, are considering merging downstream interests in the US and overseas. The deal could create one of the world's largest refining and marketing businesses and a chain of petrol stations to compete with Shell and Exxon.
-- BSKYB SEEKS PAY-PER-VIEW DEAL WITH CABLE

Satellite television operator BskyB and Cable and Wireless Communications are in talks over co-operation on the launch of pay-per-view television. Any deal could mark a turning point in the hostile relationship between BSkyB and the cable industry. Cable and Wireless Communications is a newly quoted groupings of cable companies and telephone business Mercury.
-- NatWEST TOWER IS REBORN

The tallest building in the City, the NatWest Tower, is set to be renamed tomorrow as part of a marketing campaign by National Westminster Bank to let the property. NatWest has spent 100m stg repairing and renovating the building after it was damaged by an IRA bomb in 1993.
MAIL ON SUNDAY
-- BATTLE OVER CONTROL OF HIGH STREET

Three separate consortiums are rumoured to be interested in High Street retail company Sears. US securities house Merrill Lynch attempted to buy 25 million Sears shares last week on behalf of one of the possible bidders.
-- RITBLAT SET TO BID 2BN STG FOR MEPC

British Land is set to bid 2.2bn stg for MEPC in a deal which would create Britain's biggest property company. MEPC has been a bid candidate since its talks with property group Hammerson fell through in March.
-- RAIL CHIEF IN 15-YEAR FRANCHISE ULTIMATUM

South West Trains will tell the new government it will rule out large-scale investment unless its seven-year franchise is extended. SWT chief executive Brian Cox has ambitious plans for park-and-ride stations, new trains and services.
-- ALLIED BATTLING A 24BN STG GIANT

Allied Domecq may forge closer links with Suntory of Japan in response to the proposed merger between Guinness and Grand Metropolitan. Suntory could distribute Allied brands in Japan for a return of the profits.
-- BA PLANS 'STRIKE BUSTER' FORCE TO BEAT SHUTDOWN

British Airways has made contingency plans, including a scheme to recruit hundreds of new staff at short-notice, if cabin staff vote to strike later this month. Union members believe BA will use an airline called Flying Colours to break the strike and keep Gatwick and Heathrow Airports open.
